sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Groningen makes street parking dear and tells residents that streets are for everyone, not for cars. The council adopted the 2026 parking-tax ordinance on 12 November 2025, with the levy starting on 1 January 2026: 5.00 euros an hour in the Binnenstad, Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 24:00 and Sunday from 12:00 to 17:00, and 4.50 euros in the inner ring of districts [0]. The city page shows 4.50 euros in De Hoogte, Korrewegwijk and Oosterparkwijk and 2.70 euros in outer districts, with neighbourhood-centre car parks charging 0.50 euro for the first 1.5 hours [1]. A resident permit costs 394.20 euros a year in the Binnenstad, 135.05 euros in the second zone and 62.05 euros in zones three to five [2]. Under the implementing rules, in force in consolidated form from 1 January 2026, permits per area are capped at 100% of the paid spaces, with a waiting list once the cap is reached [3]. The city lists as principles that streets are for everyone, that more room for greenery, play and cycling means parking gets less room, and that earning money is not the aim; it is installing fewer pay machines [5].

Inside the Diepenring, Westerhaven and Sledemennerbuurt a zero-emission zone applies to vans and trucks, with cameras and fines of 120 euros for vans, and an exemption transition until 2030 [6]. In the car-free area of the inner city motor vehicles may drive only between 05:00 and 12:00 for loading [7]. A study on the Diepenring aims at less traffic, less parking and more greenery on the ring road; a stakeholder session was held in January 2026 and no decision is recorded [8]. Several permit areas were merged in April 2025 and a charging permit and shared parking permit were introduced [4].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The main change is the Haddingestraat car park. The city took it over in early 2025 after it was closed to cars in January and is preparing its demolition; the design 'Harthof', with homes, small commercial uses and underground bike parking, scored highest with the public and the assessment committee, and construction is expected from 2027 [9]. The city has five park-and-ride sites: Haren/A28 (825 spaces), Hoogkerk (991), Kardinge (780), Meerstad (400) and Reitdiep (300), free to park with a return bus ticket for up to five people at about 6 euros [15]. Public chargers cost 49.44 cents per kWh, and residents who cannot get a parking permit and cannot charge at home can apply for a charging permit [17].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Since 1 August 2026 P1, part of Q-Park Netherlands after Q-Park took over APCOA Netherlands earlier in 2026, manages the municipal garages Boterdiep, Circus, Damsterdiep, Euroborg and Station Europapark, while Forum stays with Interparking [10]. The municipal garages charge 1 euro per time block with a daily maximum, for example 24 euros at Forum, 22 at Damsterdiep and 12 at Circus [11]. Q-Park lists Museum Centrum, Oosterpoort, Ossenmarkt, Rademarkt, Westerhaven and P+R Hoofdstation, the largest being Westerhaven with 734 spaces [12]. The city's Parkeren050 site shows live free-space status per garage [13], and says most neighbourhood garages are full [14]. At the Euroborg stadium car park a flat 7 euros applies on football match days [16].

Our data cover one garage with 258 spaces, a Q-Park P+R Hoofdstation, measured for 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 57% on weekdays and 49% at weekends, and reached full in a single Wednesday-morning reading. This is one of ten garages and says little about the centre as a whole. The window includes the end of the summer holidays.
